title: Route Adjudicator: incremental policy compiler and fallback-variant safety suite
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: The current routing policy codebase mixes validation, normalization, and runtime compilation in a single path which makes small changes risky and causes subtle regressions when introducing fallback model variants or new region affinity rules. We also lack an automated way to detect when a policy change will route traffic to an incompatible model variant (e.g., quantized variant without KV cache support), or when tier routing inadvertently starves lower-priority tiers during burst windows.

Goal: Implement a Route Adjudicator: an incremental policy compiler that separates parsing, typed-IR generation, and runtime contract checking. Deliver a fallback-variant safety suite that runs both static checks and lightweight runtime emulation to verify compatibility across: model capabilities, kv-cache expectations, quantization constraints, and regional deployment affinity. Output should be a machine-readable contract with compatibility flags and deterministic fallback order used by the serving runtime and orchestration layer.
technical_notes:
Design highlights:
- New staged pipeline: parse DSL -> produce typed IR -> run contract checks -> emit deployable artifacts (json contracts + metrics hooks).
- Introduce a "compatibility profile" concept that flags model variants with capabilities: kv_cache, streaming, max_tokens_local_kv, quantization_profile, multi_gpu_shardable. Profiles are strings attached to model catalog entries and used by the compiler.
- Incremental compile: cache typed-IR per-policy-hash and revalidate only diffs to reduce CI time.
- Safety suite: static analyzer (schema + semantic checks) + sandboxed runtime emulator that replays representative request traces (sampled from Console traces) against routing decisions to detect capacity/tier starvation and wrong-variant selection.
- Compatibility shim: when an older policy references deprecated selectors, the compiler emits a compatibility advisory and a best-effort rewrite suggestion.
- Expose detailed failure reasons as structured codes so Console can render actionable remediation steps.

Implementation notes:
- Language: keep the front-end parser in Typescript (policy-editor/tooling) and move the typed-IR and contract checks into Go (policy-service) for runtime parity and performance.
- Data artifacts: compiled contracts are JSON schema v2 with a version field. Each contract includes a list of route clauses, effective selectors, and an ordered fallback list with reason codes.
- Backwards compatibility: runtime will fall back to legacy validator when contract version mismatch detected; new contracts are staged via canary rollout to Dedicated nodes only initially.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end pipeline compiles sample policy corpus (existing 1200 policies) within CI budget (<20s incremental on small change).
2) Safety suite identifies at least 3 classes of regressions during fuzzing (incompatible variant, kv-cache mismatch, tier starvation) and produces actionable failure codes.
3) Serving runtime can consume compiled contracts and apply fallback ordering deterministically.
4) Console displays contract diagnostics and suggested fixes for top 10 most common failure codes.
5) A/B rollout demonstrates zero user-facing routing errors in canary region over 24h before full rollout.
migration_plan:
Phase 1: Land parser and typed-IR generation in feature branch; run compile against snapshot of current policy corpus in CI and generate contracts in artifact storage.
Phase 2: Implement compatibility profiles and static checks. Run safety suite offline, ship diagnostics to PM/Design to craft Console views.
Phase 3: Wire serving runtime to accept optional contract payload; implement graceful fallback to legacy validator when contract absent or version mismatch.
Phase 4: Canary rollout to Dedicated clusters (low-traffic customers) for 48h, collect metrics: route-mismatch, fallback-invocations, latency impact.
Phase 5: Full rollout and deprecate legacy runtime validator after 4 weeks of stable metrics.

Rollback: contracts are immutable; runtime will revert to legacy validator if contracts are disabled or a critical failure is detected. All contract artifacts are versioned in S3 with prefix "contracts/v2/".
test_plan:
- Unit tests: parser edge cases, typed-IR invariants, profile compatibility matrix (>800 test vectors).
- Integration: CI job that compiles the entire policy corpus and runs safety-suite emulation with sampled traces (Nightly).
- Fuzzing: random policy generator + property-based tests to ensure compiler never emits ambiguous fallback ordering.
- Load tests: validate compile time under concurrent policy updates (50 parallel edits).
- Canary monitoring: custom Dashboard with metrics: compiled_contract_count, compile_latency_p50/p95, fallback_invocations_by_reason, tier_starvation_alerts.
- Acceptance will include manual review session with PM/Design and runtime owners to validate Console explanations and remediation links.
